findings: Normal menu reuses the same preference lookup and omits new metadata unless choiceState=1; no new ordinary GET SQL.
The new optional query argument defaults to the same pool on normal bindingForBot calls; temporary path supplies one transaction client for own connection validation, clone and INSERT IF ABSENT.
Choice insert conflict rolls back the clone in the same transaction, does not upsert the user's existing preference.
Restore reauthenticates via existing route; DELETE includes owner/workspace/bot/stored binding/xmin/api null and active bot existence.
True absence is target; derived fallback/availability is not substituted for explicit row restoration.
Driver records exact stored binding receipt before selection validation, fails closed without receipt, and existing case loop breaks on incomplete cleanup.
Known receipt plus uncertain restore response permits one read-only absence confirmation, never a guess-based delete.
Draft preserves all P scoped quiet guards and the existing explicit chosen model restoration branch.

testFindings: All old test assertions retained; points fixture moved before first lazy import, required existing hosted-choice migration added only to isolated test schema.
Real SQL tests assert exact stored receipt, no overwrite, clone rollback, wrong scope/receipt rejection, same-value new xmin, API replacement preservation, and concurrent calls with one winner.
Route export test exercises normal GET/PUT, opt-in presence, temporary/restore responses, strict payload rejection, auth, origin and bot-scope denial with explicit mocked boundaries.

Driver adds six cases: server absence preflight, stored binding receipt restoration, preflight race, lost/incomplete initial receipt, same-value revision conflict, and one bounded read after a lost restore response.

Menu counting proxy measures the explicit pool passed to botModelMenu, not all internal settings.pool calls; equal opt-in preference reads plus unchanged source control flow establish no added ordinary query.

reservationAudit.conclusion: With the explicit stored per-bot binding, botModel returns it without rewriting the choice and bindingForBot returns the existing per-bot binding. These normal reservation calls do not themselves advance choice.xmin. Source evidence only.
